Importantly, for games where the number of available actions is large in
the original game logic, such as Dou Dizhu or HUNL, we divide a single
decision into multiple environment steps to accommodate the maximum
number of available actions within the game horizon.

### G.1 Abrupt Phantom Tic-Tac-Toe and Abrupt Dark Hex 3

#### Token Dictionary.

- •
  Token 1: Initial token
- •
  Token 2--4: Row token $`0\dots 2`$
- •
  Token 5--7: Column token $`0\dots 2`$
- •
  Token 8--9: Player token $`0\dots 1`$

#### Binary Channels.

- •
  Channel 0--8: Unobserved cells: $`0\dots 8`$
- •
  Channel 9--17: Cells $`0\dots 8`$ occupied by player 0
- •
  Channel 18--26: Cells $`0\dots 8`$ occupied by player 1
- •
  Channel 27--28: Turn indicator for player $`0\dots 1`$

#### Observation Tokens.

The game starts with an initial token (Token 1). Then, after each move
made by the player, they observe three tokens: a row token r, a column
token c, and a player token i. These tokens indicate that playing at the
corresponding cell was successful if the player token matches the
current player, or that the cell was already occupied by the other
player if the player token belongs to them. After each opponent’s move,
the player does not observe anything.

#### Action Tokens.

Each available action corresponds to a placement at an untried cell and
is encoded by the corresponding row token r and column token c.

#### Rewards.

The winning agent is awarded $`+1`$, the losing agent is awarded $`-1`$,
and both receive $`0`$ in the case of a draw.

### G.2 Liar’s Dice with 2 Dice of 5 Faces

#### Token Dictionary.

- •
  Token 1: Initial token
- •
  Token 2--3: Player token $`0\dots 1`$
- •
  Token 4: Bid token
- •
  Token 5: Call token
- •
  Token 6--10: Face tokens for $`1\dots 5`$
- •
  Token 11--15: Quantity tokens for $`0\dots 4`$

#### Binary Channels.

- •
  Channel 0--10: Last bid: $`1\dots 4`$ of face $`1\dots 5`$, or no bid
  yet
- •
  Channel 11--15: Private die 0 shows face $`1\dots 5`$
- •
  Channel 16--20: Private die 1 shows face $`1\dots 5`$
- •
  Channel 21--22: Turn indicator for player $`0\dots 1`$

#### Observation Tokens.

The game starts with an initial token (Token 1). For each dice roll, the
player observes two tokens: a face token f and a player token i,
indicating the result of each die. After any player’s bid, the player
observes four tokens: a player token i, the bid token (Token 4), a
quantity token c, and a face token f. These tokens indicate that the
corresponding player is making a bid for a certain quantity of the
specified face.

#### Action Tokens.

Each bidding action corresponds to four tokens: a player token i, the
bid token (Token 4), a quantity token c, and a face token f, which
exactly match the observation tokens. The call action consists of two
tokens: a player token i and the call token (Token 5).

#### Rewards.

The winning agent is awarded $`+1`$, the losing agent is awarded $`-1`$.

### G.3 Dou Dizhu

#### Token Dictionary.

- •
  Token 1: Initial token
- •
  Token 2--4: Player tokens – Landlord, Peasant 1, Peasant 2
- •
  Token 5--8: Discard Class – Solo, Pair, Trio, or Quad
- •
  Token 9--11: Discard Class – Straight, Pair Chain (Pair Sisters), or
  Trio Chain
- •
  Token 12: Discard Class – Rocket
- •
  Token 13--27: Rank tokens – 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, T, J, Q, K, A, 2, B,
  R
- •
  Token 28--38: Sequence starting point – 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, T, J, Q,
  K
- •
  Token 40--50: Sequence end point – 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, T, J, Q, K, A
- •
  Token 51: No kickers
- •
  Token 52--56: Solo kickers with $`1\dots 5`$ cards
- •
  Token 57--60: Pair kickers with $`1\dots 4`$ cards
- •
  Token 89: Pass token
- •
  Token 90: Hold token³³ 3 Remark: Some token indices are left empty due
  to internal backward compatibility.

#### Binary Channels.

- •
  Channel 0--53: Self-remaining cards for each card
- •
  Channel 54--107: Landlord public cards for each card
- •
  Channel 108--161: Landlord discarded cards for each card
- •
  Channel 162--215: Peasant 1 discarded cards for each card
- •
  Channel 216--269: Peasant 2 discarded cards for each card
- •
  Channel 270--284: Prefix-filling bomb count
- •
  Channel 285--287: Turn indicators for Landlord, Peasant 1, and Peasant
  2

#### Observation Tokens.

The game starts with an initial token (Token 1). In the next $`17`$
timesteps, each of the $`17`$ private cards is revealed to each player
privately using three tokens: a player token i, the hold token
(Token 90), and a rank token $`r`$. In the following $`3`$ timesteps,
the three Landlord public cards from the remaining of the deck are
announced to all players using three tokens: the Landlord token
(Token 2), the hold token (Token 90), and a rank token $`r`$.

During gameplay, the card combinations are encoded across multiple
timesteps, depending on the complexity of the card combination.

- •
  Solo/Pair combinations are encoded in one timestep with three tokens:
  a player token $`i`$, the Solo token (Token 5) or the Pair token
  (Token 6), and the rank token $`r`$.
- •
  Trio/Quad combinations are encoded in multiple timesteps. The first
  timestep contains three tokens: a player token $`i`$, the Trio token
  (Token 7) or the Quad token (Token 8), and the major rank token $`r`$.
  In the second timestep, the kicker details are specified, and the
  token count increases to four by including the kicker information.
  This can be no kicker (Token 51), one solo kicker (Token 52) or one
  pair kicker (Token 57) for a trio, or two solo kickers (Token 53) or
  two pair kickers (Token 58) for a quad. The following timesteps encode
  each kicker as if they were discarded individually as a solo or pair,
  in increasing order.
- •
  Straight/Pair Chain combinations are encoded in two timesteps. The
  first timestep contains three tokens: a player token $`i`$, the
  Straight token (Token 9) or the Pair Chain token (Token 10), and the
  sequence starting point token $`r_{1}`$. In the next timestep, the end
  point of the sequence is determined, and four tokens are presented,
  including the sequence end point token $`r_{2}`$.
- •
  Trio Chain combinations are encoded in multiple timesteps. The first
  timestep contains three tokens: a player token $`i`$, the Trio Chain
  token (Token 11), and the sequence starting point token $`r_{1}`$. In
  the second timestep, both the kicker information and the sequence end
  point are specified together. For a Trio Chain with kickers (airplane
  with wings), the token sequence contains five tokens, including the
  sequence end point token $`r_{2}`$ and the kicker information. The
  following timesteps encode each kicker as if it were discarded
  individually as a solo or pair, in increasing order.
- •
  Rocket is encoded in one timestep with two tokens: a player
  token $`i`$ with Rocket token (Token 12).
- •
  PASS is encoded in one timestep with two tokens: a player token $`i`$
  and the pass token (Token 89).

Under this multi-timestep decision encoding, the maximum number of
actions required in one timestep is significantly reduced to $`35`$
actions, compared to $`27{,}472`$ in DouZero \[[7](#bib.bib13)\].
Notably, the channels are updated as if the kickers were treated as
continuous actions by the player: a Trio Chain with three pair kickers
is treated as first discarding a Trio Chain with kickers, followed by
three additional timesteps for discarding each kicker, which are limited
to pairs.

#### Action Tokens.

The action tokens are identical to the observation tokens as the actions
are public.

#### Rewards.

Let $`B`$ be the total number of quads and rockets played during
gameplay. The Landlord is awarded $`+2\times 2^{B}`$ if they win, and
$`-2\times 2^{B}`$ if they lose. Each Peasant is awarded
$`+1\times 2^{B}`$ if they win, and $`-1\times 2^{B}`$ if they lose.

### G.4 Heads-Up No-Limit Texas Hold’em

#### Token Dictionary.

- •
  Token 1: Initial token
- •
  Token 2--14: Rank tokens – 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, T, J, Q, K, A
- •
  Token 15--18: Suit tokens – c, d, h, s
- •
  Token 19--21: Action tokens – Fold, Call, Raise
- •
  Token 22--25: Street tokens – Preflop, Flop, Turn, River
- •
  Token 26--27: Player tokens – Small Blind, Big Blind
- •
  Token 28--75: Amount tokens – Raise to $`i\times 16^{j}\times 10`$
  chips ($`0.1`$ big blinds)
- •
  Token 76: Raise all-in

The raise tokens encode 3 base-16 digits, specifically following
amounts: 0, 10, 20, 30, …, 150, 160, 320, 480, …, 2560, 5120, 7680, …,
40960 chips.

#### Binary Channels.

- •
  Channel 0--33: $`2\times 17`$ channels for the two hole cards: suits
  c, d, h, s then ranks 2..A
- •
  Channel 34--118: $`5\times 17`$ channels for the five board cards,
  same as private hands
- •
  Channel 119-170: self hole cards, 52-card multi-hot
- •
  Channel 171--222: visible board cards, 52-card multi-hot
- •
  Channel 223--246: Total pot, 6 base-4 digits
- •
  Channel 247--270: Current player’s bet on this street, 6 base-4 digits
- •
  Channel 271--294: Opponent’s player’s bet on this street, 6 base-4
  digits
- •
  Channel 295--296: Turn indicator for Small Blind and Big Blind

#### Observation Tokens.

In the encoding, each card dealt is encoded over two timesteps: the rank
token is presented in the first timestep, while the suit token is
presented in the second timestep. This reduces the number of branches
from 52 cards to 13 ranks, as we treat the board dealer as a special
player for deterministic transitions.

The game starts with an initial token (Token 1). The next $`2\times 2`$
timesteps reveal the two hole cards to each player *simultaneously*.
After each betting round, the corresponding board cards are revealed,
with each card taking two timesteps.

For a board card, the first timestep contains one token, the rank token
$`r`$, while the second timestep contains two tokens: the rank token
$`r`$ and the suit token $`s`$. For a private hole card, the
corresponding player token $`i`$ is also attached to the encoding, so
the number of tokens becomes two and three respectively.

In the betting rounds, actions are encoded over multiple timesteps
depending on the complexity of the action. For a raise action, the
sequence is encoded using three timesteps, each timestep decides one
digit of the base-16 numbers. Specifically, in an all-in raise, the
raise sequence is replaced by the all-in token.

The other actions, Call/Check and Fold, are encoded using three tokens
in one timestep, containing a street token, a player token $`i`$ and
either the Call token (Token 20) or the Fold token (Token 19).

The environment faithfully represents all trajectories, since actions
are never aggregated. The only exception is that, within each betting
street, the fifth raise is constrained to be an all-in raise to avoid
excessively long training episodes.

#### Action Tokens.

The action tokens are identical to the observation tokens as the actions
are public.

#### Rewards.

The players are awarded a chip change measured in big blinds. Since
there are $`20{,}000`$ chips in the stack, the maximum reward is
$`200`$.

exploitability over random seeds, with uncertainty shown as

bold the best mean within each game block.

### J.3 PPO Clipping Coefficient

We finally inspect the effect of the base clipping coefficient
$`\varepsilon_{\mathrm{base}}`$ used in the PPO-style policy update. We
sweep the coefficient over
$`\varepsilon_{\mathrm{base}}\in\{0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2\}`$ and present the
results in
Table [8](#A10.T8 "Table 8 ‣ J.3 PPO Clipping Coefficient ‣ Appendix J Ablation Study on General Hyperparameters ‣ GAE Falls Short in Imperfect-Information Self-Play Reinforcement Learning").
Smaller clipping coefficients impose a tighter constraint on policy
updates, while larger values allow more aggressive updates.

Across all three games, VRPO achieves its best performance at a clipping
coefficient of $`0.02`$. Increasing the coefficient generally degrades
VRPO, especially at $`0.2`$, suggesting that overly loose policy updates
can hurt stability in these exact-exploitability benchmarks.

## Appendix K Ablation Study on VRPO-specific Hyperparameters

We study the effect of VRPO-specific hyperparameters on the overall
performance of VRPO.

### K.1 Replay Buffer Capacity

We inspect the effect of changing the replay buffer capacity
$`|\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{replay}}|`$. We sweep the ratio between the
capacity of replay buffer $`|\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{replay}}|`$ and the
rollout batch size $`|\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{rollout}}|`$ over
$`\{1,4,16,64\}`$, and present the results in
Figure [14](#A11.F14 "Figure 14 ‣ K.1 Replay Buffer Capacity ‣ Appendix K Ablation Study on VRPO-specific Hyperparameters ‣ GAE Falls Short in Imperfect-Information Self-Play Reinforcement Learning").
While a higher ratio means the critic is trained on more diverse
samples, it also introduces additional lag between the stored
trajectories and the current policy. When the ratio is $`1`$, VRPO
reduces to using only the current rollout to update the critic without
replay, following the standard PPO training scheme.

As shown in the figure, increasing the replay buffer capacity does not
degrade performance. In our experiments, we set the replay buffer
capacity to $`64\times|\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{rollout}}|`$ to balance
sample divergence and total memory consumption.

Figure 14: Exact exploitability (lower is better) of agents in APTTT
(Abrupt Phantom Tic-Tac-Toe), ADH3 (Abrupt Dark Hex 3), and LiDi 2D5F
(Liar’s Dice with 2 Dice and 5 Faces), trained with VRPO under different
replay buffer capacity.

### K.2 Number of Critic Epochs

We inspect the effect of changing the number of critic epochs
$`K_{\mathrm{critic}}`$ per iteration. We sweep
$`K_{\mathrm{critic}}\in\{1,2,4,8\}`$ and present the results in
Figure [15](#A11.F15 "Figure 15 ‣ K.2 Number of Critic Epochs ‣ Appendix K Ablation Study on VRPO-specific Hyperparameters ‣ GAE Falls Short in Imperfect-Information Self-Play Reinforcement Learning").
As shown in the figure, a larger number of critic epochs leads to a more
accurate critic, resulting in more stable performance, as expected. In
our main experiments, we set $`K_{\mathrm{critic}}=4`$ to balance
stability and computational cost, matching the PPO baselines used in
CleanRL \[[25](#bib.bib17)\].

Figure 15: Exact exploitability (lower is better) of agents in APTTT
(Abrupt Phantom Tic-Tac-Toe), ADH3 (Abrupt Dark Hex 3), and LiDi 2D5F
(Liar’s Dice with 2 Dice and 5 Faces), trained with VRPO under different
numbers of critic epochs.
